target_customer: Employers paying to recruit college students and recent graduates for internships and entry-level jobs
problem: Employers struggled to reach and engage students and early-career candidates, while students found general job boards aimed at older workers.
business_model: Two-sided marketplace with employers paying for recruiting products; free for students

founders.name: Liz Wessel
founders.background_notes: Per her YC profile she was CEO and cofounder for 7.5 years through the exit; later a partner at First Round Capital.

founders.name: JJ Fliegelman
founders.background_notes: Only the title is on the YC page.

exit.acquirer: Yello (combined company; Yello is the legal entity)
exit.reason: Combined to add automation and analytics workflows to WayUp's diverse candidate pipeline; terms undisclosed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A job marketplace with profiles, matching and applications is standard web engineering. Later machine learning matching was an enhancement, not a requirement.

defensibility.rationale: Student supply and employer demand create modest network effects, but employers use several channels and campus recruiting rivals such as Handshake grew faster, per 2021 coverage.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Neither copied the niche in a way that stopped WayUp. Handshake became the stronger rival, and WayUp combined with Yello in 2021.

market_need_then: By late 2015 a CNN profile reported more than 150,000 registered students at 2,400 colleges, indicating student demand. Employers seeking early-career talent were the paying side.

branding.name_origin: Renamed in August 2015 from Campus Job. The company says students read the old name too literally and it limited expansion beyond campus jobs. Two Cornell interns came up with WayUp after an advisor-led naming session produced no result.
branding.domain_note: Company uses wayup.com; how it was acquired was not found.

identity.logo: Designed by students hired from the platform, per the company's account

branding.brand_signature: A rebrand story in which the company hired its own student users to name and design the brand

rebrands.why: The old name was constantly misnamed, read too literally as on-campus jobs, and limited expansion beyond the college world

branding.community_and_virality: A campus rep and student ambassador program was part of the model, and the rebrand was covered by TechCrunch. No evidence of merch or meme culture.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear, positive name replaced a confusable one, helping with expansion, and the brand was kept as a separate brand under Yello in 2021, but WayUp was not a category-defining brand against Handshake.

pivots.from: Campus Job: part-time campus jobs and campus rep roles
pivots.to: WayUp: entry-level jobs and internships for students and recent graduates
pivots.why: Scope had widened beyond campus jobs and the old name did not fit

outcome_analysis: WayUp grew from a campus jobs site into an early-career marketplace, renamed itself in 2015, raised an $18.5M Series B led by Trinity in 2017 and later reported a database of more than 6 million candidates. It ended by combining with Yello in July 2021 with undisclosed terms. Its growth stalled relative to Handshake, so the exit looks like a consolidation by a mid-sized player in a market where a better funded rival grew faster.
notes: Competition left empty: sources naming LinkedIn, Indeed and Handshake are from 2017 to 2021, not near founding; LinkedIn and Indeed are named as rivals in the 2017 TechCrunch piece. Earlier investors named there (RRE Ventures, Y Combinator, Eniac Ventures) lack amounts and dates, so no seed round is recorded. Series A is reported at $9M by Wikipedia and $7.8M by Clay (search snippets); unverified, so not recorded as a round. A search snippet cites a PR Newswire release for the Series B that I did not open. Founder education and prior employers were not found in opened sources. Status Acquired on YC conflicts with exit type merger; Yello is the legal entity and both brands persist. WayUp acquired Looksharp in February 2017 (search snippet). A cumulative total of $27.5M is stated in TechCrunch.
